text:
Amira (Product): @here Quick heads-up — next Tue 2026-04-07 we are enabling "Secure Default Mode" for all NEW Private/VPC deployments and running a coordinated "Agent Repair Day" to assist existing customers with the upgrade and config migration. This is a change to defaults (not a forced change to customer data) but it will flip on stronger security defaults for new installs and staged opt-in for older installs.

Amira (Product): TL;DR impact:
- New installs: TLS enforcement, KMS auto-rotation enabled, telemetry default = opt-out (customers can re-enable).
- Existing installs: no automatic breaking changes; support window to assist in applying the new defaults starting the same day.
- Agent auto-upgrade to agent-v3.2.1 will be offered (not forced) during Agent Repair Day.

Amira (Product): Why: reduces customer risk surface, aligns with SOC2/FedRAMP expectations, and simplifies our default support posture for private installs.

Noah (Security): Short note on compliance: enabling KMS auto-rotation by default means customer-managed keys will keep the same policy but we recommend customers with strict rotation windows check their KMS policies. This does not change access controls or export rules.

Sanjay (Eng): For Eng/Infra: the opt-out toggle for telemetry and the single-command agent upgrade are available in the ops kit: https://go.redwood.internal/onprem/secure-defaults-runbook (internal). Agent upgrade command we will use for the assist flow:
```bash
redwood-agent upgrade --version v3.2.1 --batch 50
# or for k8s
kubectl apply -f https://go.redwood.internal/agents/v3.2.1/daemonset.yaml
```
If there are mass failures we'll roll back with the previous image tag and open the incident channel.

Lisa (Customer Success): CS playbook is on the runbook page — we'll send a notification email to customers in the next 48h and include the opt-out link and scheduled assist windows. We'll also surface customers with custom KMS or air-gapped installs (they get manual outreach).

Amira (Product): Checklist for teams (short):
- Product: confirm messaging and support FAQ (done).
- CS: send notif + schedule pre-check calls for flagged customers.
- Eng: enable the assist automation and monitor upgrade telemetry.
- Security: confirm rotation alerting and DPA wording.

Noah (Security): Note: legal asked that we include the DPA addendum link in the email for customers who want to accept rotation defaults now.

Sanjay (Eng): Monitoring endpoints to watch during the assist: /agent/upgrade/status, /telemetry/ping, and per-tenant connection metrics. Pager rules have been added to the release runbook.

deploy-bot: deploy-triggered: ops/agent-assist/2026-04-07 initiated by Amira. Rollout window: 03:00-09:00 UTC.

Lisa (Customer Success): :white_check_mark: Sending the first wave of emails today EOD to customers in the US and EU who opted into managed updates.

Amira (Product): Thanks all. If you own a private-customer path, please review the runbook and raise issues in #eng-oncall immediately. We will post a post-mortem template if anything unexpected occurs. :thumbsup:

Noah (Security): If anyone needs me for customer calls next week, ping me — I'll be on standby.

Sanjay (Eng): Will post a short troubleshooting snippet for kernel/networking incompatibilities by EOD.

Amira (Product): Closing note: this is intentionally conservative — no forced key changes or data rotation will happen server-side. We're aiming for safer defaults and a low-friction assist experience.
